answer:
An ETF’s expense ratio isn’t usually charged as a separate fee to your account. The fund pays its operating expenses from its assets, so those costs gradually reduce the ETF’s net asset value and returns.

For example, a 0.20% annual expense ratio on a $10,000 investment is about $20 per year, reflected over time—not typically billed as a $20 transaction. Your actual cost varies with your investment’s value and holding period.

Trading commissions, bid–ask spreads, and taxes are separate costs and aren’t included in the expense ratio.
